title: Stable reordering + continuation token design for rerank endpoint
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: Current reranking endpoints return items in descending score order but do not guarantee deterministic ordering for equal-score items, and the pagination model (offset-based or inconsistent cursors) leads to duplicate/skipped items under concurrent updates and non-deterministic developer UX. We need a clear, backwards-compatible API that: (1) gives deterministic stable ordering, (2) supports an efficient continuation token for paginated reads that is monotonic and compact, (3) exposes per-item provenance for auditability, and (4) enables streaming partial results with safe resumption. This ticket defines the design, API examples, trade-offs, rollout strategy, and acceptance criteria for the new model.
proposed_api_examples:
1) Synchronous request (simple top-k):
Request:
POST /v2/rerank?mode=rank&continuation_type=cursor
{
  "query": "how to reset password",
  "documents": [ { "id": "doc:1", "text": "..." }, { "id": "doc:2", "text": "..." } ],
  "k": 10
}

Response:
{
  "items": [
    { "id": "doc:2", "score": 0.8423, "provenance": "ann_candidate:27|cross_score:0.8423", "stable_key": "00000000a1f3" },
    { "id": "doc:1", "score": 0.8423, "provenance": "ann_candidate:5|cross_score:0.8423", "stable_key": "00000000a1f4" }
  ],
  "continuation_token": "eyJ2IjoiMSIsImxhc3Rfc2NvcmUiOjAuODQyMywibGFzdF9zdGFibGUiOiIwMDAwMDAwMGExZjQiLCJzZWVkIjoxNTQzMjM0NTY3fQ==",
  "more_available": false
}

2) Streaming partial rerank (for very large candidate sets):
Request: stream=true&k=50
Response: chunked stream of structured items; final chunk contains continuation_token and more_available flag.

3) Continuation token (opaque base64 JSON) decoded example:
{
  "v": "1",
  "last_score": 0.8423,
  "last_stable_key": "00000000a1f4",
  "seed": 1543234567
}
Note: token versioning allows future changes (v2 may include sharding metadata).
design_decisions:
1) Stable ordering: sort by (score DESC, stable_key ASC). stable_key is deterministic per-item and produced by hashing a canonical id+insertion_ts+model_version; this guarantees stable ordering across repeated calls and safe resumptions.

2) Continuation token: opaque base64-encoded JSON with fields (v, last_score, last_stable_key, seed). Using last_score+last_stable_key provides an exact resume point for inclusive-exclusive continuation without relying on offsets. Token is compact, versioned, and signed with a server secret to prevent tampering.

3) Support for explicit-k and windowing: clients can request k (final number of results returned) and optionally window_size to control server candidate buffer/batching behavior. Server may fetch extra candidates for dedup and tie-breaking; window_size is an advisory parameter for performance tuning.

4) Provenance and structured output: each item includes a small provenance string and optional structured fields: {embedding_index, retrieval_stage, cross_encoder_score, raw_components}. We keep provenance as a short pipe-delimited string for backward compat but allow a richer structured_provenance field in v2 tokens.

5) Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming returns early shallow results with more_available true and a continuation_token; non-streaming will block until top-k exact set is determined. Streaming is required for large-scale search where initial latency is critical.

6) Backwards compatibility: existing clients without continuation_type or using offset will continue to work with an internal translation layer (server will support offset for one release cycle but mark deprecated).
tradeoffs:
- Deterministic stable_key generation adds small CPU/IO cost at ingestion; but avoids complex server-side tie-breakers and nondeterministic UX.
- Opaque signed tokens reduce client-side flexibility (clients cannot edit token), but simplify server validation and protect from invalid cursors.
- Streaming introduces complexity around partial dedup and consistency when underlying corpus changes between pages; document must clearly warn clients: high churn sources may see shifted results.
- Exposing provenance increases response size; we will keep a compact provenance string by default and enable a verbose mode.
- Cursor-based pagination prevents random-access jumps cheaply (offset remains useful for small datasets); we will deprecate offset for large datasets but keep it temporarily for compatibility.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (alpha): implement server-side stable_key generation, basic cursor token v1, and structured item response (compact provenance). Expose behind feature flag and run internal dogfood queries.

Phase 2 (beta): add streaming endpoint, support token signing, add translation layer for offset -> cursor, and create SDK helpers (JS/Python) to decode/inspect tokens. Run canary on 10% of traffic and run regression evals.

Phase 3 (GA): enable for all customers with transition docs. Deprecation notice for offset-based pagination with a 6-month timeline. Provide migration guide and client samples.

Rollback: if we detect increased duplicates or >0.5% error spike in rerank paths, flip feature flag and fall back to current ordering until root cause is fixed.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for stable_key generation across id permutations.
- Property tests to ensure ordering invariants: for identical inputs, order is stable across repeats.
- Integration tests: resume-from-token yields same full ordered sequence as single-shot request.
- Load tests: p95 end-to-end latency for k<=10 must be < 75ms for typical datasets at 1000 RPS on dedicated hardware. For streaming large candidate sets, first-chunk latency p95 < 120ms.
- Chaos tests: simulate document insertion/deletion between pages to validate dedup safeguards and user-visible warnings.
- Compatibility tests: offset translation layer returns equivalent results for small datasets.
- Backward compatibility: ensure older SDKs get same item order when token absent.
- Security tests: token tampering detection and signature verification.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Deterministic order guarantee: for a stable corpus and identical request parameters, repeated calls return identical item sequences (automated tests pass).
2) Cursor resume fidelity: concatenating pages via returned continuation_token reproduces the same ordered sequence as single-shot top-N request (tests).
3) Latency: p95 end-to-end latency for typical 10-item rerank <= 75ms in our canary environment.
4) Provenance: every returned item contains a provenance field; verbose_provenance available behind parameter.
5) Backwards compatibility: legacy offset parameter returns consistent results and is supported for one release cycle with deprecation warnings.
6) Documentation and SDK helpers published (JS/Python) and migration guide available.
7) Security: continuation tokens are cryptographically signed and verified; invalid tokens return 400.
8) Observability: console dashboard includes token usage metrics, token decode failure rate, and cursor-driven request traces.
notes:
- Consider adding a server-side optional deterministic seed parameter so clients can request stable random tie-breaking when using learning-to-rank ensemble inputs.
- We should coordinate with the console team to show 'cursor' examples in the rerank route docs and surface token decode helpful info in dev mode.
- Check GDPR/PII implications of including insertion_ts in stable_key generation; use non-reversible hashing and avoid raw timestamps in token payloads.
- Discuss with SDK owners whether to expose a decode_inspect(token) helper that returns a redacted JSON for debugging only (disabled in production SDK builds).
